purpose: Adversarial high-entropy stress test of exact Glyphin memory encodings.
key_observation: Under this deliberately high-entropy fixture family, both structural encodings retained exact state fidelity while state-columnar produced the highest mean token reduction (53.61%), structural-lineage produced 52.52%, and sim17-compact produced 35.80%.
interpretation: The structural advantage survived the adversarial entropy benchmark, but the result is benchmark-specific evidence only. It is not evidence of a global optimum, universal superiority, or an 80% token reduction guarantee.
referee_note: Children ordering is treated as a derived index and compared as a set; all other state fields and memory parameters remain exact comparison targets.
